variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Start in A when the execution scene shows an empty, open gripper. At this first decision, identify the demonstrated peg by gripper closure followed by sustained co-motion during the initial lift. Determine whether its head or tail was grasped from that closure and lift, and trace that endpoint back to its unobscured pre-contact position. Continuous motion evidence overrides a conflicting late held-object label on an endpoint that stayed stationary; such a label must not change the identified peg or grasp end. Match the identified peg and endpoint to the reset execution scene and point to that endpoint's current visible position, not a shifted or occluded centroid during demonstration contact.  When the current execution observation shows a peg held after pickup, switch from A to B if insertion_side is "right", or to C if insertion_side is "left". Accept an explicit held-object label as evidence of a successful grasp only when consistent with the observed motion. Closure followed by sustained co-motion of the peg with the raised hand is sufficient evidence of a successful grasp, even when the wrist later leaves the frame. A conflicting label on a stationary endpoint does not override that evidence, and the wrist being outside the frame does not imply an empty hand. B and C require no point. Do not choose insertion side from the current pickup location. The demonstrated insertion command completes the supplied episodes; no subsequent menu transition is required. For an unanticipated decision, prioritize visible state: if still holding a peg, use the remembered insertion side; if that value is "unknown", use the side of the box on which the held peg currently lies, choosing B for smaller x and C for larger x. If empty-handed and a demonstration remains visible, reapply the demonstrated pickup rule. If empty-handed with no demonstration available, choose A at the clearest accessible peg endpoint as a best-effort fallback rather than claiming to recall an unrecorded target.

fields.name: insertion_side
fields.description: When the current observation includes the demonstration and incoming memory is empty, isolate the demonstration's final low-height approach into the box. Identify the carried peg by gripper closure followed by sustained co-motion during the initial lift, and track that peg and its gripper into the final approach. Continuous motion evidence overrides conflicting held-object labels on stationary pegs. Compare the carried peg/gripper's x position on the approach side with the box's x coordinate: x greater than box x means "left"; x less than box x means "right". Classify the side from which it approaches, not the direction of motion: motion toward smaller x from larger x is insertion from robot-left, not robot-right. These labels are robot-relative, not camera-relative. If the peg disappears into the box, use the last clearly visible approach before occlusion, not the final occluded frame. Ignore the original pickup location, the high transport path (including any crossing over the box), and the reset execution scene when assigning the side. Write this value at the first decision. Write "unknown" only if the demonstration genuinely does not establish an approach side. At steps without a demonstration, copy the incoming value unchanged; do not infer a new side from the currently held peg's location. e.g. "right"
fields.annotation: Record the demonstrated insertion side, as "right" or "left", at the first decision step and retain it at every subsequent step. Determine the side from the peg's final approach into the box, not from its original pickup location: approach from smaller x than the box is robot-right; approach from larger x is robot-left. Episodes 1, 15, and 60 have "right" at both steps; episodes 33 and 54 have "left" at both steps. This is the only retained fact: the demonstrated peg and grasp end are available when pickup is selected, and the successful grasp is visible at the next decision. e.g. "right"

history.critique:
field insertion_side, POLICY PROMPT
  When asked to repeat the demonstrated peg, grasp end, and insertion side, the policy correctly selected the demonstrated tail but wrote "right" even though the demonstrated final insertion approached from larger x than the box and the annotation was "left". In one case the pickup began at smaller x and crossed over the box before insertion; in the other the pickup and insertion were both at larger x. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure in applying the side-extraction rule, not a missing memory field. Strengthen the existing rule with an explicit comparison: at the first decision, isolate the demonstration's final low-height approach toward the box, track the carried peg and its gripper rather than stationary pegs, and compare their x coordinates with the box's x coordinate. An approach from larger x moving toward smaller x is "left"; an approach from smaller x moving toward larger x is "right". These are robot-relative labels, not camera-relative labels. Ignore the initial pickup location, high transport path, and reset execution scene when assigning this value. If the peg disappears into the box, use the last clearly visible approach before occlusion rather than requiring a visible peg in the final frame. For example, a carried peg approaching from x around 195 toward a box at x around 148 establishes "left", even if it was picked up near x 99. Write this value at the first decision and copy it unchanged at subsequent decisions. Retain "unknown" only when the demonstration genuinely does not establish the approach side.

refused
  The two failed first decisions selected the same demonstrated tail endpoints as the recorded pickup commands, with points differing by only a few pixels: visible reset endpoint centers rather than slightly displaced recorded target points. These do not select different objects or grasp ends, so they do not establish a SUFFICIENCY failure under the object-selection criterion. Do not add coordinate offsets, memorized target points, or episode-specific pickup rules. The existing pickup rule already calls for the demonstrated endpoint in the current reset scene. The annotation's left-side values also agree with both demonstrations and the existing annotator prompt, so no annotation change or additional retained fact is warranted.

history.critique:
field insertion_side, POLICY PROMPT
  At the initial decision, the instruction required reproducing the demonstrated insertion side. In demonstrations where the carried peg approached the box from larger x while moving toward smaller x, the policy wrote "right", although the annotated value was "left". The selected pickup endpoint was otherwise correct. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure in applying the robot-relative mapping, not a missing memory fact. Strengthen the existing rule with an explicit two-case check: during the final low-height insertion approach, carried peg/gripper x greater than box x means "left"; carried peg/gripper x less than box x means "right". Motion toward smaller x does not mean insertion from the right: it means approaching from the larger-x, robot-left side. Establish the carried object's identity by closure and sustained co-motion, ignoring conflicting labels on stationary pegs. Use the last unoccluded approach if necessary, excluding pickup and high transport. Write the resulting value when the demonstration is visible with empty incoming memory, for example "left", and copy it unchanged at subsequent decisions. Do not change the field or its annotation values.

the policy prompt for subgoal
  When the instruction required picking the same end of the same demonstrated peg, the gripper closed on a head and that peg subsequently moved with the raised hand. Near insertion, an unrelated stationary tail was labeled held. The policy selected that stationary tail in the reset scene instead of the demonstrated head, even though insertion_side was correctly recorded as either "left" or "right". This exposes a SUFFICIENCY failure in the policy prompt's evidence precedence for identifying the pickup target, not a need for additional memory. Amend the demonstrated-pickup rule to identify the peg from closure followed by sustained co-motion during the initial lift, determine the grasped endpoint from that closure and lift, and trace that endpoint back to its unobscured pre-contact position. Match that peg and endpoint to the reset scene and select its current endpoint. Explicitly state that continuous motion evidence overrides a conflicting late held-object label on an endpoint that stayed stationary; such a label must not switch the demonstrated target or grasp end. Replace the unconditional claim that an explicit held-object label establishes a successful grasp with a rule accepting that label when consistent with the observed motion, while retaining closure followed by co-motion as sufficient evidence even when the wrist later leaves the frame. Keep the held-peg insertion rules: B for remembered "right", C for remembered "left", with no point. Remove episode-specific pickup examples as decision rules; use the general closure, co-motion, and reset-matching procedure instead.

refused
  The two incorrect-side outputs also used pickup points slightly different from the recorded points, but both selected the correct demonstrated tail in the reset scene. These differences do not justify coordinate-specific corrections: sufficiency requires selecting the correct object and endpoint, not reproducing an identical pixel. No annotation-field change or additional retained peg/end field is warranted. The insertion-side annotations agree with the visible final approach, the demonstration is available when pickup is chosen, and the successful grasp is visible when insertion is chosen.
